intro: You are standing on Beycesultan, a mound in Denizli province whose story begins in 5000 BC. With forty settlement layers, it is among the deepest mounds in western Anatolia, and its Bronze Age palace was a centre of the land the Hittites called Arzawa.
history: Forty settlement layers lie stacked here, making this one of the deepest mounds in western Anatolia. Its Bronze Age palace points to one of the centres of the land the Hittites called Arzawa in their correspondence. Excavation began in the 1950s and continues, campaign by campaign.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Bronze Age palace and the megaron buildings, then look for the room with altars and the Chalcolithic levels.
facts: Did you know? The palace's burnt layer shows that it was abandoned suddenly, and the fire itself preserved what was left inside. With forty settlement layers, Beycesultan is among the deepest mounds in western Anatolia.
outro: This brings our journey through Beycesultan to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
